item.title: Reverse a Function: hand-rolled strcmp
item.description:
Challenge: Target Windows x86-64 (MSVC calling convention: first pointer arg in rcx, second in rdx, return in eax). Reverse this short function to equivalent C:
mystery: xor eax, eax loop_top: movzx r8d, byte ptr [rcx] movzx r9d, byte ptr [rdx] cmp r8d, r9d jne diff test r8d, r8d je done inc rcx inc rdx jmp loop_top diff: mov eax, r8d sub eax, r9d ret done: ret
What does mystery(const char *a, const char *b) compute?
Answer:
int mystery(const char *a, const char *b) { while (*a == *b) { if (*a == 0) return 0; a++; b++; } return (unsigned char)*a - (unsigned char)*b; }
It's a hand-rolled strcmp: byte-by-byte comparison that stops at the first mismatch or shared null terminator.
Explanation: movzx r8d/r9d, byte ptr [...] zero-extends each byte read so the later sub produces the classic unsigned-byte-difference result strcmp returns. jne diff breaks out on the first mismatching byte; test r8d,r8d / je done catches equal bytes that are both the string's null terminator, returning 0 (eax was zeroed up front). The inc rcx / inc rdx pair advances both pointers in lockstep, mirroring the C loop's a++; b++;.
